entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philopoemen was a skilled Greek general and statesman, who served as Achaean strategos on eight occasions from 200 to 182 BCE.

He played a significant role in the Achaean League's struggles against the Roman Republic, particularly during the Third Macedonian War.

Philopoemen's leadership and military prowess earned him great respect among his peers, but his personal life was marked by controversy and scandal.

Despite his flaws, Philopoemen remains a fascinating figure in ancient Greek history, offering insights into the complexities of Greek politics and society during the Hellenistic period.

His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Roman policy towards Greece and shaping the course of Mediterranean history.
